questions.stem: NASA sends a robotic rover to Mars rather than human astronauts for an initial mission. Which is the most scientifically valid reason for this choice?

options.text: Robots are better at doing science experiments than humans
Robotic missions do not need to carry life support, food, or return fuel, making them much lighter, cheaper, and less risky
Humans cannot survive the journey to Mars under any circumstances
There is no scientific value in sending humans to Mars

questions.explanation: Robotic missions are significantly cheaper and less risky because they do not need life support systems, food, water, or fuel for a return journey. They can also withstand conditions (radiation, extreme temperatures) that would be dangerous for humans. Humans can potentially survive a Mars journey (C is too absolute), and human exploration has scientific value (D). While robots have limitations compared to humans for some tasks, the key advantage is reduced cost, weight, and risk (A overstates robot capabilities).

questions.stem: A signal is sent from Earth to a Mars rover. Mars is currently 1.5 AU from Earth. If 1 AU equals approximately 8 light-minutes, roughly how long does the signal take to reach Mars?

options.text: 8 minutes
12 minutes
1.5 minutes
120 minutes

questions.explanation: If 1 AU corresponds to 8 light-minutes, then 1.5 AU corresponds to 1.5 x 8 = 12 light-minutes. Radio signals (used for communication) travel at the speed of light. This means there is a 12-minute delay each way, so a round-trip command-response takes about 24 minutes. This communication delay is one reason Mars rovers must have some autonomous capability. Option A is the Sun-Earth distance only. Option C divides instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: The Hubble Space Telescope is in orbit above Earth's atmosphere. What is the main advantage of placing a telescope in space rather than on the ground?

options.text: It is closer to the stars, so they appear bigger
There is no atmosphere to absorb or distort light, giving clearer and sharper images across all wavelengths
It can see further because there are no buildings blocking the view
It uses a bigger mirror than any ground telescope

questions.explanation: Earth's atmosphere absorbs certain wavelengths of light (like infrared and ultraviolet) and causes distortion (twinkling) of visible light. A telescope in space avoids these problems, producing much sharper images and being able to observe wavelengths that cannot penetrate the atmosphere. The orbital altitude (A) is negligible compared to stellar distances. Ground telescopes can be larger (D). Buildings are not the relevant obstruction -- the atmosphere is (C).

questions.stem: Which method of space exploration allows scientists to study distant galaxies billions of light years away?

options.text: Sending robotic probes to fly past them
Landing rovers on them
Using ground-based and space-based telescopes to collect electromagnetic radiation from them
Sending astronauts to observe them up close

questions.explanation: Galaxies billions of light years away are far too distant for any probe or crewed mission to visit -- even at the speed of light, it would take billions of years. The only way to study them is by collecting the electromagnetic radiation (light, radio waves, X-rays, etc.) they emit, using telescopes on Earth or in orbit. Probes (A) and rovers (B) can only reach objects within our Solar System. Human space travel (D) has only reached the Moon.

questions.stem: Long-duration human spaceflight (such as a mission to Mars) presents several health challenges. Which of the following is a genuine health concern caused by the microgravity environment in space?

options.text: Astronauts grow extra fingers due to radiation exposure
Bone and muscle loss, because the body no longer needs to support itself against gravity
Astronauts' lungs stop working because there is no air pressure in the spacecraft
Astronauts become permanently unable to see colours

questions.explanation: In microgravity, bones and muscles are not loaded as they are on Earth, leading to significant bone density loss and muscle atrophy. Astronauts on the ISS exercise for about 2 hours daily to combat this. Spacecraft are pressurised, so breathing is normal (C). Growing extra fingers (A) and permanent colour blindness (D) are not real effects of spaceflight. Other genuine concerns include radiation exposure, cardiovascular changes, and fluid redistribution.
